title: Applied ML — Rotor Brief (week of 2027-06-28)
body:
Purpose:
This brief captures the Applied ML weekly research standup for the 'Rotor' onboarding track (compact-precision experiments + eval hygiene). Focus for this week: 3-bit/4-bit quant probes for 7B/13B model family, end-to-end eval regressions observed in canned QA sets, and a KV-cache regression discovered on Dedicated clusters after the recent runtime kernel swap.

High-level summary:
- Progress: Completed second pass of 3-bit symmetric quant for 7B (channel-wise outlier clipping), ran baseline evals on the small-sweep prompt suite. Microbatch tuning (batch_size=8->16) improved throughput ~18% for 7B int4 flows without breaking latency SLOs.
- Regressions: Noticed BLEU-like drop on summary evals vs FP16 baseline for 13B-int3 probes (~6% relative decrease for a subset of commonsense prompts). Investigating whether this is a quantization artifact or eval-flakiness.
- Production impact: KV-cache invalidation bug causes occasional +40ms tail latency spikes on Dedicated when a cold-start model variant is loaded in the same GPU pod. Mitigation: pin-old-kernel fallback route enabled for affected customers while we patch.

Detailed notes (by day):
Mon 2027-06-28:
- Ran channel-wise outlier detection + per-channel rescaling for the 7B MLP layers. Observed decreased per-token perplexity on LM-mini dev set (ppl: 12.8 -> 12.0).
- Spike reproduced locally when running long-context (>2048) scoring with mixed packing. Started a small root-cause triage with SRE.

Tue 2027-06-29:
- 13B int3 sweep: ran 24 configs (per-layer bit allocation, outlier thresholds). Config 13B-C3 (higher precision for attention q/k) retains fluency but fails in factual QA slices. Hypothesis: attention quantization skew.
- Began building an evaluation harness to isolate attention vs MLP quant noise.

Wed 2027-06-30 (standup):
- Mateo ran eval drift check across last 3 checkpoints; drift visible only when sequences include code-like tokens. Action: add token-type stratification to eval dashboards.
- Priya repro'd KV-cache invalidation on Dedicated: sequence of model reload -> request with stale cache -> cache miss triggers a large memcpy on GPU that stalls the batching worker. Patch PR opened (see linked PR).

Thu 2027-07-01:
- Microbatch tuning: Luca validated that increasing microbatch packing window to 120ms reduces overall token cost by ~12% for interactive workloads with burstiness. Needs follow-up to ensure fairness for small-req customers.
- Samir ran adversarial prompt set (privacy & instruction-following) on quantized 7B models; small increase in hallucinations for int3 in narrow instruction prompts.

Experiment log (short):
- Experiment: 7B-CW3 (channel-wise 3-bit, outlier clip 2.5 sigma)
  - Config id: ROTOR-7B-CW3-A1
  - Runtime: dedicated-dev GPU (a100-40)
  - Eval passes: LM-mini dev, rotor-canned-50, instruction-adversarial-10
  - Result: Perplexity -6.3% vs int4 baseline; latency +2ms; hallucination delta +0.8% (within noise)

- Experiment: 13B-ATT4/MLP3 hybrid
  - Config id: ROTOR-13B-HYB-01
  - Result: Factual QA F1 -6% on 'wiki-fact' subset; immediate suspicion on attention Q/K quant perturbation

Metrics snapshot (select):
- 7B int4 throughput: 860 tokens/s (baseline fp16: 720 tokens/s) on a100-40 with microbatch=12
- 7B int3 probe throughput: 1050 tokens/s (but increased instability in KL-estimates)
- Tail latencies (p95 p99) for Dedicated after kernel swap: p99 increased from 210ms -> 250ms on avg.

Blockers / open issues:
- KV-cache invalidation patch needs post-merge observability checks; root cause may be an allocator edge-case in newest memory manager. Currently blocked on infra to repro reliably in staging.
- 13B int3 factual drop: need a reproducible minimal test that isolates attention quantization.
- Eval flakiness: some decrease tracked to shuffled dataset ordering between runs; we need deterministic seed convention in harness.

Decisions made:
- Roll-forward plan: keep pin-old-kernel fallback enabled for Dedicated customers who hit p99 regressions until patch rolled and validated by SRE (expected timeline: 72 hours).
- Quant policy: for now, prefer hybrid precision for 13B (higher bits for attention q/k, allow lower for MLP) until attention quant stability confirmed.

Action items (owner / due):
- Arielle: complete deterministic-eval-harness (seed, dataset stratification) and land in GH by 2027-07-06. (blocker: none)
- Mateo: reproduce 13B-attention-only quant test and log per-layer activation distributions; due 2027-07-04.
- Priya: follow-up on KV-cache PR, add extra memcheck and timing hooks; due 2027-07-02.
- Luca: run fairness microbench for microbatch=120ms window across 10 customer-like traces; due 2027-07-07.
- Samir: assemble adversarial prompt fuzz set for quant-safety testing (50 seeds); due 2027-07-05.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Try per-head selective precision for 13B attention (low-cost probe: int2 for heads with low L2 norm).
- Add a short-run 'cache-warm' shim to the serving runtime for Dedicated that does a lightweight validation request after model load to avoid first-traffic tail spikes.
- Consider adding sequence-type labels (code / instruction / chat) to eval dashboards to catch axis-specific regressions earlier.

Meeting follow-ups planned:
- Deep-dive (technical) with SRE & infra: 2027-07-02 11:00 PT — KV-cache triage and staging repro plan.
- Quant review sync: 2027-07-06 09:00 PT — present hybrid-precision findings and 13B attention isolation tests.

Appendix (quick links & artifacts):
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4827 (KV-cache fix + mem hooks)
- Eval harness draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AMP/Rotor-Onboarding-Notes
- JIRA ticket: AMP-1192 (Rotor onboarding - quant regressions)

End of brief.

(Notes: this doc is intentionally lightweight, contains working hypotheses and dev action items. Will convert to a more formal postmortem if KV-cache root cause is confirmed.)
